page: Amazon Web Services r8id.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, utilizing the Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with x86_64 architecture running at 3.9 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, supplemented by a 480 MB L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512, AMX-tile, AMX-int8, and SHA extensions. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB of DDR5 running at 7 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Discrete GPUs are not included on this instance type. Direct-attached storage is provisioned as a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD, and networking provides a baseline throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-threaded compute efficiency. In Geekbench single-core testing, the instance scores 2156.0, placing in the top quartile, alongside upper-tier compression benchmarks including 34.41 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 14.33 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Text processing results are similarly elevated at 2805.0. Conversely, multi-threaded compute reflects physical core constraints, with stress-ng multi-core (4321.26) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (28.7 GB/sec) settling in the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth, static web serving (8.36 GB/sec), and database tasks like Redis SET operations (7.61 million operations per second) demonstrate median performance.

The r8id.xlarge offers resource density suited for workloads requiring substantial memory and rapid local disk access without overpaying for excessive CPU cores. Tradeoffs include modest total multi-threaded bandwidth and a 2 Gbps network baseline. As configured, the instance aligns closely with in-memory caching systems, distributed key-value stores, session management layers, and localized data processing queues.
description: Amazon Web Services r8id.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance driven by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, and a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Single-core throughput is strong, ranking in the top quartile for Geekbench single-core tests and gzip compression, aided by extensive instruction support including AVX-512 and AMX matrix extensions. However, multi-core scaling is modest due to the physical core count, and network throughput provides a 2 Gbps baseline. With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high-speed local disk, the r8id.xlarge offers an efficient footprint for in-memory key-value databases, session caching layers, text processing, and intermediate storage pipelines that demand significant memory capacity without high core counts.
